templates.name: Explosive strength — Beginner four-week reference
templates.purpose: Give the workout-generation model an exercise-based progression reference for explosive strength, not a mandatory athlete program.

selection_rules.use: Select methods matching the athlete's sport demand, environment, equipment and level; preserve the category objective and weekly progression shape.
selection_rules.avoid: Do not include every listed method, invent a method, progress multiple loading variables at once, or use fatigue as proof of effectiveness.
selection_rules.session_order: Complete relevant preparation first; perform speed, power and high-skill work before fatiguing strength or conditioning; place low-priority capacity work later.
selection_rules.dose_application: The weekly prescription applies to the primary_reference method. Preparation and supporting references use their own released method-dose compatibility; they must not inherit the primary dose blindly.

weeks.progression_condition: Complete the planned exposure with acceptable technique/output, no pain or illness, and no material interference with the next key sport session.
weeks.regression_condition: If quality, readiness, symptoms or schedule gate fails, repeat the prior successful week or use the category regression; do not progress automatically.

templates.exercise_progression_policy: Keep the reference methods stable across four weeks and progress dose or execution quality first. A method change requires the stated progression gate, a compatible substitution, and no new equipment or level conflict.
templates.week_4_policy: Consolidation/deload by default. It may become an assessment or competition week only when the sport package and athlete schedule explicitly require it.

templates.ai_use: Reference for one-call four-week generation. AI may adapt within released method eligibility and dose bounds; it must not copy blindly or exceed constraints.
templates.prompt_reference_text: Explosive strength — Beginner four-week reference. Approved method candidates: Standing Jump-and-reach, Underhand Throw. Use this as a flexible exercise-based planning reference: Week 1 (entry and establish baseline): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 3 at fast, submaximal, with 120s recovery. Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 4 at fast, with 120-150s recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 4 sets/series × 3 at high quality, with 150s recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 3 at high quality, with 120s recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.

Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 5 sets/series × 3 at maximal safe intent, with 180-240s recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 5 sets/series × 2 at maximal safe intent, with 240s recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 2 at high quality, with 180s recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.

selection_rules.use: Select methods matching the athlete's sport demand, environment, equipment and level; preserve the category objective and weekly progression shape.
